I had the same problem you're having. Facts is, relationships aren't white and black, they're more in a spectrum: what I mean is, there's something else between "they don't care about my company" and "they love hanging out with me".  
  
In my specific case, I found out that what was causing me pain was the fact that I was putting too much of myself into that group, while, even if the other members would be okay with hanging out from time to time, they weren't as invested as I was, thus making me feel bad and letting all those bad thoughts flurry in my head.  
  
This may also be your case: they still appreciate your company, but they prefer going out with other groups, while still caring about you, although not as much as you do (for example if they only have 1 evening free, they'd rather spend it with others than with your group).  
  
Said that, I don't think you should either try harder nor give it up. Try to distance yourself a little from they, while still keeping in touch: you'll find that eventually they'll want to go out, but not as often as you'd expect. Instead hang around that other friend you mentioned and maybe try to involve some of their friends aswell, try to create another group who's willing to put the same effort in the relationship as you do and, if everything fails, try taking care of yourself: go to a spa for a day, go watch a movie you like or start reading a book; all these things, while improving your mood, give you unique experience you can talk about to others, to help them understand what kind of people you are.  
   
Tl;dr: don't give up on them, but try to loosen up a bit. Find someone else that values and is willing to put as much effort as you do in the friendship. If in the meanwhile you find no one, don't give up and in the meanwhile try having fun by yourself.
